vuln.catalogue.title: Vulnerability catalogue
vuln.catalogue.text:
One entry per vulnerability, shared by every case, registry entry and war room: public CVE, GitHub (GHSA) or vendor advisories, and private entries for issues found in your own investigations.

Every signed-in user can read, add and edit entries. Merging and deleting entries is for server administrators. The counts show only the cases you can open and the registry entries of customers you are associated with.

vuln.identifier.title: Identifier
vuln.identifier.text:
A public entry is named by its CVE, GHSA or advisory identifier (CVE ids are stored in upper case). An identifier is unique ignoring letter case, and it cannot also be another entry's identifier or alias.

A private entry gets IRIS-VULN-<year>-<number> when it is saved; that identifier never changes and the number is never reused.

vuln.private.title: Private entry
vuln.private.text: For an issue that has no public identifier, such as a misconfiguration or a weakness found during an investigation. It is numbered IRIS-VULN-<year>-<number> and never leaves this instance. Whether an entry is private is chosen when it is created.

vuln.kind.title: Kind
vuln.kind.text: What sort of issue this is. Automatic picks CVE for a CVE id, Advisory for any other public identifier and Other for a private entry.

items.name: CVE
items.text: A vulnerability published with a CVE id.

items.name: Advisory
items.text: A vendor or GitHub (GHSA) advisory without a CVE.

items.name: Misconfiguration
items.text: A setting that exposes a system, not a software flaw.

items.name: Weak credentials
items.text: Default, shared or guessable credentials.

items.name: Exposed service
items.text: A service reachable where it should not be.

items.name: Design flaw
items.text: A weakness in how a system or process is built.

items.name: Zero-day
items.text: Exploited before a fix or advisory exists.

items.name: Other
items.text: Anything else.

vuln.cvss.title: CVSS
vuln.cvss.text:
A CVSS vector (2.0, 3.0, 3.1 or 4.0) sets the version and the base score. A score typed next to a vector wins, for an environmental or temporal score.

The severity follows the score (0 none, under 4 low, under 7 medium, under 9 high, then critical) unless you choose one by hand; choose Automatic to make it follow the score again.

vuln.epss.title: EPSS
vuln.epss.text: FIRST's Exploit Prediction Scoring System: the probability that the vulnerability is exploited in the next 30 days, and how that ranks against all scored CVEs (the percentile). Enter both as percentages, with the date they were taken; they are not fetched automatically.

vuln.kev.title: CISA KEV
vuln.kev.text: Listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue: exploitation in the wild is confirmed. Record the date it was added, the remediation due date CISA set for US federal agencies, and whether it is known to be used in ransomware campaigns.

vuln.exploit_maturity.title: Exploit maturity
vuln.exploit_maturity.text: How far exploitation of this vulnerability has gone, anywhere - not in your environment (that is a finding's exploitation status).

items.name: Unknown
items.text: Not assessed.

items.name: None known
items.text: No public exploit is known.

items.name: Proof of concept
items.text: A demonstration exploit exists.

items.name: Weaponized
items.text: A working exploit is available, for example in a framework.

items.name: In the wild
items.text: Attackers are exploiting it (a KEV listing implies this).

vuln.patch.title: Patch availability
vuln.patch.text: Whether the vendor offers a fix.

items.name: Unknown
items.text: Not assessed.

items.name: Patch available
items.text: A fixed version or patch exists.

items.name: Workaround only
items.text: Only a configuration change or mitigation is offered.

items.name: No fix
items.text: The vendor offers nothing yet.

vuln.products.title: Affected products
vuln.products.text: One product per line: vendor | product | versions, for example Apache | httpd | 2.4.49 - 2.4.50. The vendor and the versions may be left out. The catalogue's Vendor and Product filters read these lines.

vuln.aliases.title: Aliases
vuln.aliases.text: Other identifiers of the same issue, for example the GHSA id of a CVE. Searching or quick-adding by an alias finds this entry, and a CVE IOC whose value is an alias links to it. A merge adds the merged entry's identifier and aliases here.

vuln.cve_org.title: cve.org
vuln.cve_org.text:
For a CVE, Fill from cve.org reads the public CVE record and fills the form: title, description, CVSS, CWEs, affected products, references, dates, and from CISA's data the KEV listing and the exploitation status. Only the CVE id is sent.

Sync refreshes an entry. A value you changed since the last sync is kept unless you choose to overwrite it. Settings -> System turns lookups off.

vuln.merge.title: Merge
vuln.merge.text: For two entries that describe the same issue. The findings and war-room tracking of the entry you merge move to the target; where the target already has a finding on the same asset, the two are folded into the target's (status and notes appended to its notes). The merged entry's identifier and aliases become aliases of the target, and it is deleted. Server administrators only; it cannot be undone.

vuln.exposure.title: Exposure
vuln.exposure.text: Where this vulnerability is recorded: case findings, registry entries, and cases that hold its identifier or an alias as a vulnerability IOC. Only the cases you can open and the registry entries of customers you are associated with are counted and listed.

vuln.finding.title: Finding
vuln.finding.text: A vulnerability recorded where it matters to you: on one of a case's assets or on a customer's registry entry. One finding per vulnerability and asset. A finding has its own remediation and exploitation status, owner, due date and history; the catalogue entry holds what is true everywhere.

vuln.remediation.title: Remediation status
vuln.remediation.text: Where fixing it stands (CISA VEX). The statuses fall in three groups: open, fixed and dismissed. Risk accepted and False positive need a reason.

items.name: Under analysis
items.text: Open: not yet known whether the asset is affected.

items.name: Affected
items.text: Open: the asset is vulnerable.

items.name: Mitigated
items.text: Open: a workaround reduces the risk; the fix is still due.

items.name: Patched
items.text: Fixed: the fix is applied.

items.name: Verified
items.text: Fixed: the fix is confirmed (rescan, manual check); records who verified it and when.

items.name: Not affected
items.text: Dismissed: the asset is not vulnerable; give the VEX justification or a reason.

items.name: Risk accepted
items.text: Dismissed: knowingly left as it is; needs a reason.

items.name: False positive
items.text: Dismissed: the detection was wrong; needs a reason.

vuln.exploitation.title: Exploitation status
vuln.exploitation.text: Whether this vulnerability was exploited on this asset. Exploited at (UTC) is kept only while the status is Exploited.

items.name: Unknown
items.text: Not assessed.

items.name: Not exploited
items.text: Checked, and no sign of exploitation.

items.name: Attempted
items.text: Exploitation was tried and failed.

items.name: Suspected
items.text: There are signs, not proof.

items.name: Exploited
items.text: Confirmed; record when.

vuln.vex.title: VEX justification
vuln.vex.text: Why the asset is not affected, in CISA VEX terms. Used with Not affected only.

items.name: Component not present
items.text: The vulnerable component is not installed.

items.name: Vulnerable code not present
items.text: The component is there but without the vulnerable code.

items.name: Vulnerable code not in execute path
items.text: The code is present but never runs.

items.name: Vulnerable code cannot be controlled by adversary
items.text: An attacker cannot reach or influence it.

items.name: Inline mitigations already exist
items.text: Existing protections stop exploitation.

items.name: Version not affected
items.text: The installed version is outside the affected range.

items.name: SaaS deployment
items.text: Fixed by the provider of a hosted service.

items.name: On-Prem deployment
items.text: The on-premises deployment is not exposed as described.

vuln.due.title: Due date
vuln.due.text: When the fix should be in place. An open finding past its due date shows as overdue.

vuln.links.title: Linked events and IOCs
vuln.links.text: The case's timeline events and IOCs that relate to this finding, for example the event where exploitation was seen. Only items of the same case can be linked.

vuln.history.title: Finding history
vuln.history.text: Every change to a finding: the field, the old and new value, who changed it and when (UTC). It is kept until the finding is deleted.

vuln.asset_tab.title: Asset vulnerabilities
vuln.asset_tab.text: The vulnerabilities recorded on this asset, with their status. The tab counts the open ones; in the asset list a shield shows the same count, coloured by the most severe open vulnerability. Recording or changing a finding needs full access to the case. Every vulnerability of the case, across its assets: Intel > Vulnerabilities with the Case filter.

vuln.case_filter.title: Case filter
vuln.case_filter.text: Shows only the entries recorded on an asset of the chosen case; the Exposure column then counts that case's findings. The list offers the cases you can open that hold findings. With Affected, only entries still open in that case.

vuln.registry.title: Registry vulnerabilities
vuln.registry.text: Vulnerabilities recorded on this registry entry, independent of any case - for example the results of a scan of the customer's estate.

vuln.war_room.title: Vulnerabilities in a war room
vuln.war_room.text: Tracked: the entries the room is following, with the room's note on each (responders and leads change them). Across the room's cases: every vulnerability recorded in the cases attached to the room that you can open, with open / recorded counts per case.

vuln.ioc_link.title: CVE IOCs
vuln.ioc_link.text: An IOC of type vulnerability whose value is a catalogue entry's identifier or alias links to that entry, and the entry's exposure lists the case. Nothing is created automatically: to track the vulnerability in the case, record a finding.

vuln.lookup_setting.title: Look up CVEs on cve.org
vuln.lookup_setting.text: When on, the vulnerability catalogue can fill and refresh CVE entries from cve.org (the CVE Services record), through the proxy configured on the General tab. Only the CVE id is sent, and only when someone asks. Turn it off for air-gapped deployments.
